q: The area of a square is d. What is the area of the circle which has the diagonal of the square as its diameter?
explanation: Side² = d, so the diagonal² = 2d, and the diagonal is the circle's diameter. Radius² = diagonal²/4 = d/2, so the circle's area = πr² = (1/2)πd.

q: Which one of the following is a closed form expression for the generating function of the sequence {aₙ}, where aₙ = 2n + 3 for all n = 0, 1, 2, … ?
Let ⊕ and ⊙ denote the Exclusive OR and Exclusive NOR operations, respectively. Which one of the following is NOT CORRECT?
explanation: P ⊕ ¬P is always 1, so the left side reduces to 1 ⊕ Q = ¬Q. P ⊙ ¬P is always 0, so the right side reduces to 0 ⊙ ¬Q = Q. Since ¬Q ≠ Q in general, option (D) is the one that is NOT correct.

q: Consider a matrix A = uvᵀ where u = (1, 2)ᵀ, v = (1, 1)ᵀ. Note that vᵀ denotes the transpose of v. The largest eigenvalue of A is _____.
explanation: A = uvᵀ is a rank-1 matrix, so its only nonzero eigenvalue equals trace(A) = u·v = (1)(1) + (2)(1) = 3.

q: Consider the sequential circuit shown in the figure, where both flip-flops used are positive edge-triggered D flip-flops. The circuit is a 2-bit shift register with input 'in' feeding the first flip-flop, whose output feeds the second flip-flop's D input, both driven by the same clock, with 'out' taken from the second flip-flop. The number of states in the state transition diagram of this circuit that have a transition back to the same state on some value of 'in' is _____.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"><rect x="70" y="30" width="60" height="50"/><rect x="170" y="30" width="60" height="50"/><line x1="20" y1="55" x2="70" y2="55" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs22)"/><line x1="130" y1="55" x2="170" y2="55" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs22)"/><line x1="230" y1="55" x2="270" y2="55" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs22)"/><line x1="20" y1="110" x2="270" y2="110"/><line x1="100" y1="110" x2="100" y2="80" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs22)"/><line x1="200" y1="110" x2="200" y2="80" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs22)"/></g><defs><marker id="ah2018cs22" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><text x="6" y="50" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">in</text><text x="235" y="50" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">out</text><text x="10" y="125" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">clock</text><text x="82" y="60" font-size="13" fill="currentColor">D  Q</text><text x="182" y="60" font-size="13" fill="currentColor">D  Q</text></svg>
explanation: With state (Q1,Q2) and next state (in, Q1), state (0,0) self-loops when in=0 and state (1,1) self-loops when in=1; the other two states (0,1) and (1,0) never return to themselves. So 2 states have a self-loop.

q: Consider the following parse tree for the expression a#b$c$d#e#f, involving two binary operators $ and #. Which one of the following is correct for the given parse tree?
options: $ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is right associative
# has higher precedence and is left associative; $ is right associative
$ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is left associative
# has higher precedence and is right associative; $ is left associative
explanation: The $ subexpressions (b$c, then (b$c)$d) are nested deepest, so $ binds tighter than #, and its left-leaning nesting ((b$c)$d) shows left associativity; the right-leaning nesting of # (a # (... # (e#f))) shows # is right associative.

q: Consider the following undirected graph G with edge weights as shown (the top vertex connects to the left vertex with weight 4, to the right vertex with weight x, and by two diagonals of weight 1 and 3 to the bottom-left and bottom-right vertices respectively; the left and bottom-left vertices are joined by an edge of weight 4, the two bottom vertices by an edge of weight 4, and the bottom-right and right vertices by an edge of weight 5). Choose a value for x that will maximize the number of minimum weight spanning trees (MWSTs) of G. The number of MWSTs of G for this value of x is ______.
explanation: Setting x = 5 ties the top-right edge with the other weight-5 edge, and checking all spanning trees shows the minimum weight of 13 is achieved by exactly 4 different edge subsets, more than for any other value of x.

q: Given a language L, define Lⁱ as follows: L⁰ = {ε}; Lⁱ = Lⁱ⁻¹·L for all i > 0. The order of a language L is defined as the smallest k such that Lᵏ = Lᵏ⁺¹. Consider the language L₁ (over alphabet 0) accepted by the automaton shown, whose start state and the state reached after one '0' are both accepting, and from that accepting state, reading '0' leads to a non-accepting state from which reading '0' returns to the accepting state. The order of L₁ is _____.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 160" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah2018cs52" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><line x1="10" y1="80" x2="50" y2="80" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs52)"/><circle cx="70" cy="80" r="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="70" cy="80" r="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="86" y1="80" x2="164" y2="80" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs52)"/><text x="120" y="72" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">0</text><circle cx="185" cy="80" r="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="185" cy="80" r="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M199,70 C230,50 260,50 285,68" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs52)"/><text x="235" y="52" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">0</text><path d="M285,92 C260,112 230,112 200,92" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#ah2018cs52)"/><text x="235" y="118" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">0</text><circle cx="300" cy="80" r="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>
explanation: L₁ = {0ⁿ : n = 0 or n odd}, so L₁¹ misses even lengths ≥2 while L₁² already contains every length (0+0, 0+odd, odd+odd), and L₁² concatenated with L₁ again gives all lengths, so L₁² = L₁³ while L₁¹ ≠ L₁²; the order is 2.
